dek: Equifax is paying $100 million over wrong credit scores sent to lenders in spring 2022.

slides.label: The Error
slides.text: For three weeks in spring 2022, a *coding error* at Equifax sent lenders the wrong credit scores.

slides.label: The Damage
slides.text: Scores were off by as much as *20 points*, enough to get a loan, card or apartment turned down.

slides.label: The Settlement
slides.text: Equifax agreed to pay *$100 million* to settle the class action, without admitting fault.

slides.label: Who Qualifies
slides.text: About *4 million people* in the US whose Equifax data was sent to a lender between March 17 and April 8, 2022.

slides.label: Three Choices
slides.text: File a claim, do nothing, or *opt out by Nov 27* to keep your right to sue Equifax yourself.

slides.label: The Deadlines
slides.text: *Nov 27*: opt out deadline. *Dec 28*: file your claim. Payouts land after court approval in 2027.

slides.label: The Payout
slides.text: Lawyers estimate *$95 to $280 a person*, but the final number depends on how many people file.

slides.label: The Den's Take
slides.text: A three digit number *you never saw* decided who got a loan that month. Check your credit like your bank balance.

caption_instagram:
The Equifax credit score settlement is here: for three weeks in spring 2022, a coding error sent lenders the wrong scores, off by as much as 20 points, enough to get a loan, card or apartment turned down.

Equifax agreed to pay $100 million without admitting fault. About 4 million people are in the class, and if your file was pulled in that window, a notice with a claim number starting 'EFX-' should already be in your inbox or mailbox.

You get three choices: file a claim for an estimated $95 to $280, opt out by November 27 to keep your right to sue, or do nothing and get neither. Deadlines move fast, Nov 27 to opt out, Dec 28 to file.

Did a loan, card or apartment denial in spring 2022 ever not make sense to you? Send this to someone who applied for credit that year.

Equifax just agreed to pay $100 million after a coding error sent lenders the wrong credit scores for three weeks in spring 2022, some off by as much as 20 points. About 4 million people are in the class.

For founders and operators, the lesson isn't just about your own credit file. It's about how much of your business, a loan, a lease, a line of credit, rides on a number you never see and cannot check in real time. A three digit score decided who got funded that spring, and most people found out only when the answer came back no.

If your file was pulled between March 17 and April 8, 2022, you have three options: file a claim (estimated $95 to $280), opt out by November 27 to keep your right to sue, or do nothing and get neither. The claim deadline is December 28.

Have you ever had a financing decision turn on a credit number that didn't add up?
